summary: E2E Stripe payment flow tested on both backend (19/19 pytest passing) and frontend. Backend: booking-request creates Stripe Checkout with correct €270.00 amount (3 nights x €90 for Appartamento Brufani Due, 2 guests), city tax €18 separate, 409 on iCal-blocked dates and on double-booking, iCal export works, owner confirm/reject tokens validated, reject flow performs real Stripe refund (tested via PaymentIntent + stripe.Refund) and releases dates, guest status endpoint returns correct state. Frontend: successfully drove the actual Stripe test checkout (card 4242 4242 4242 4242) end-to-end for date 2027-05-10..13; booking BRF-7EB826 was marked PAID in DB, PaymentIntent pi_3UMn2FGf8LaKpPSg1ss3NZxw created, blocked dates 2027-05-10/11/12 correctly added, owner confirm link flipped status to 'confirmed' and guest status endpoint reflects it. However the frontend 'Pagamento riuscito!' success panel (data-testid=booking-success) NEVER renders in the preview environment because the polling useEffect is broken by React 18 StrictMode double-invocation (details below).

ui_bugs.issue: After Stripe redirects back to /?pagamento=successo&session_id=..., the booking-success panel is never shown and the 'Pagamento annullato' toast on /?pagamento=annullato also fails to appear reliably. Root cause: React.StrictMode is enabled in /app/frontend/src/index.js and the useEffect at BookingSection.jsx:32 runs twice in dev. First invocation reads the query, calls history.replaceState (stripping the query), sets verifying=true and starts a setInterval. The cleanup fires setInterval -> clearInterval(poll). The second invocation now reads an empty query (since replaceState already ran) and returns early at line 36, so no new poll is scheduled. Result: verifying stays true forever, setConfirmed(d.booking) never fires, toast.success never fires. In production (Vercel/Render) React doesn't double-invoke so it may work there, but preview is dev-mode and the described test case fails in it.

integration_issues.issue: DB and payment flow are both correct (polled /api/payments/status/{session_id} manually returns payment_status=paid + booking payload) but the panel never renders due to the StrictMode bug above.

Same StrictMode bug swallows the error toast on /?pagamento=annullato: cleanup runs immediately after mount, and on second mount esito is null (replaceState already stripped query), so toast.error is only fired once in-between and no visible toast is observed after 3s.

action_items: Fix BookingSection.jsx useEffect to be StrictMode-safe: either guard with a useRef flag so the effect body only runs once, or read-and-cache the session_id/esito synchronously BEFORE calling history.replaceState, store sessionId in state, and run the polling in a second effect keyed on that state. Alternatively simply persist the sessionId to sessionStorage before clearing it from the URL so a second effect invocation still finds it. Verify both the success panel and the 'Pagamento annullato' toast reappear on page refresh.
Minor: data-testid in request body says 'booking-submit-btn' but code uses 'booking-submit-button' - acceptable, but worth aligning docs.
critical_code_review_comments: BookingSection.jsx:32-69 - the useEffect is not StrictMode safe (see above).
server.py:566 - success_url uses hard-coded query key names 'pagamento' & 'session_id' in Italian; this is fine but keeps the URL language-coupled. OK.
server.py:613 _expire_stale_pending runs on every GET /availability call - could cause slow responses when many stale bookings exist. Consider making it async-non-blocking via BackgroundTasks.

server.py:729 /payments/status does NOT verify the caller owns the session (no email check). Anyone with a valid session_id can read booking details including email and dates. Low-risk because session_id is a random Stripe id, but worth noting.
BookingSection.jsx polling attempts=8 x 2s = 16s. If Stripe redirect takes longer than that the user gets 'errorGeneric'. Consider longer or exponential backoff.
No webhook idempotency protection: _mark_paid is called both from polling and webhook; the status guard 'if booking.status != pending_payment' handles idempotency correctly - good.

success_rate.frontend: 66% (payment flow + redirect works; success panel + cancel toast do not render in preview due to StrictMode bug)

test_credentials: Stripe test card 4242 4242 4242 4242, 12/29, 123 (from request). No app-level credentials used.
seed_data_creation: Created 1 real paid booking BRF-7EB826 (test.e2e@example.com, Appartamento Brufani Due, 2027-05-10..13, €270 paid via Stripe test, now status=confirmed via owner-link). Also 2 test paid bookings for confirm/reject fixtures (auto-cleaned by pytest teardown).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is solid: pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_booking_payment_flow.py (19 tests) exercises Stripe session creation, 409s, refunds, confirm/reject, guest status, iCal export. The sole bug blocking the full UX is the StrictMode double-invocation of BookingSection.jsx useEffect at line 32 which strips the Stripe session_id from the URL on first mount cleanup and never polls again. Once fixed, retest: (1) /?pagamento=successo&session_id=cs_test_a1AZPNKIYOssHbVELDhKwpvkMNbl08l7RRa4wKE00f8zsGJfZkd9XEdyI3 should show booking-success with code BRF-7EB826 (already paid+confirmed in DB), (2) /?pagamento=annullato should show the 'Pagamento annullato' toast. The remaining features in the review request (owner confirm link, dates blocked after payment, Stripe refund, iCal 409) are all verified working. Note: the booking BRF-7EB826 is permanently in DB; delete if cleanup is desired. Preview is dev-mode React; production bundle on Vercel/Render would not exhibit the StrictMode issue - but the fix must still be applied because StrictMode double-invoke semantics will be enforced in all React 19+ future production builds.
rca of the issue: Reproduction: open https://book-assisi-direct.preview.emergentagent.com/?pagamento=successo&session_id=cs_test_a1AZPNKIYOssHbVELDhKwpvkMNbl08l7RRa4wKE00f8zsGJfZkd9XEdyI3 and wait ~20s. Expected: booking-success panel with BRF-7EB826. Observed: payment-verifying stays visible indefinitely. Root cause: React.StrictMode (index.js:18) + BookingSection.jsx:32 useEffect runs twice; the first run calls history.replaceState() to strip query params before starting setInterval, cleanup immediately clears the interval, and the second run finds no params so it exits early. Fix: use a useRef guard to run the body only once, or snapshot the query params in a top-level module variable, or push session_id to state and poll in a separate effect that only unmounts on real unmount.
